```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(appusageR)
data(appusage_demo)
```

Use a temporary project to observe reuse and repair. All destructive steps below
target only files created by this example.

```{r first-run}
folder <- system.file("extdata", "synth", package = "appusageR", mustWork = TRUE)
path <- file.path(folder, appusage_demo$sources$source_relpath[1L])
work <- tempfile("appusage-recovery-")
config <- appusage_config(execution = list(parallel = FALSE, workers = 1L, progress = FALSE))
first <- run_appusage_workflow(path, project_dir = work, config = config)
stopifnot(isTRUE(validate_appusage_project(work, verify = "content")$complete))
```

## Unchanged inputs reuse completed stages

```{r resume}
elapsed <- system.time(resumed <- run_appusage_workflow(project_dir = work))
plan <- plan_appusage_workflow(project_dir = work, verify = "content")
plan$tasks[, c("stage", "action", "reason_code")]
stopifnot(all(plan$tasks$action %in% c("reuse", "disabled")))
elapsed
resumed$run_record$tasks
```

The entry point still spends time validating evidence and constructing results.
Read actual stage actions alongside elapsed time. A metadata preview is cheaper
but does not load and validate scientific content. See
`?appusage_configuration` for `source_verification` options.

## Missing JSON and damaged RDA

```{r missing-pair}
pair <- resumed$second_level[1L, ]
unlink(pair$second_level_metadata_file)
expected_warnings <- character()
record_damage_warning <- function(w) {
  message <- conditionMessage(w)
  if (grepl("cannot open file|magic number", message)) {
    expected_warnings <<- c(expected_warnings, message)
    invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
  }
}
missing <- withCallingHandlers(validate_appusage_project(work, verify = "content"),
                              warning = record_damage_warning)
stopifnot(!isTRUE(missing$complete))
repair_plan <- plan_appusage_workflow(project_dir = work, verify = "content")
repair_plan$tasks[, c("stage", "action", "reason_code")]
repaired <- run_appusage_workflow(project_dir = work)
stopifnot(isTRUE(validate_appusage_project(work, verify = "content")$complete))
```

```{r damaged-pair}
pair <- repaired$second_level[1L, ]
writeBin(charToRaw("deliberately damaged synthetic cache"), pair$second_level_data_file)
damaged <- withCallingHandlers(validate_appusage_project(work, verify = "content"),
                              warning = record_damage_warning)
stopifnot(!isTRUE(damaged$complete))
restored <- run_appusage_workflow(project_dir = work)
stopifnot(isTRUE(validate_appusage_project(work, verify = "content")$complete))
cache <- new.env(parent = emptyenv())
load(restored$second_level$second_level_data_file[1L], envir = cache)
stopifnot(identical(cache$data, appusage_demo$records$line_seven_days$data))
expected_warnings
```

A missing or damaged pair is different from a complete terminal input diagnosis.
The example records and displays the expected missing-file/invalid-RDA warnings;
any other warning is left to R's normal handler.
The planner selects the required work from compatible upstream caches; it does
not turn every source into a fresh run. `?plan_appusage_project_rebuild` offers a
metadata-only inventory for older layouts. `run_appusage_stage("summary", ...)`
rebuilds projections from valid caches; rebuilding a summary is not scientific
reprocessing.

## Inspect a partial source failure

```{r partial-input}
index <- match("invalid_interval_structure", appusage_demo$sources$scenario)
bad_path <- file.path(folder, appusage_demo$sources$source_relpath[index])
issue <- tryCatch(run_first_level_appusage(bad_path, strict = TRUE), error = identity)
stopifnot(inherits(issue, "appusage_line_structural_quality"))
conditionMessage(issue)
```

This source contains one valid interval and one interval missing its end time.
Its critical structural diagnosis is preserved, rather than publishing the valid
fragment as if it were a complete source. The next project example retains this
and four other diagnoses through an unchanged resume.

```{r cleanup}
unlink(work, recursive = TRUE)
```
